plan: Ten new items checked against the bank: derivative and erroneous WIC, portrait cross-text, squirrel-cache inference, 'that of' comparison (hard), 'Meanwhile', duration synthesis, comma after a dependent clause, seasonal-steps data, orchestra inference.

passages.title: Borrowed rhythms
passages.text: Critics agree that the young poet's first collection is largely ______: its rhythms, its images, and even several of its phrases are borrowed from the poets she most admired.

passages.title: Early charts
passages.text: Many of the earliest charts of the region were ______: they placed some islands dozens of miles from their true positions and left others off entirely, errors that later surveys corrected one by one.

passages.title: A disputed sitter (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
An art historian argues that a 1792 portrait of an unnamed young woman depicts the painter's sister, pointing to the strong resemblance between the sitter and the sister's known features.

Text 2
Letters in a family archive show that the painter's sister spent all of 1791 and 1792 abroad. The same letters mention that a neighbor sat for the painter several times during the winter of 1792.

passages.title: Hidden nuts
passages.text: Gray squirrels bury thousands of nuts each autumn and recover many of them months later. To test how they find their caches, researchers moved the large stones and logs near some caches after the squirrels had buried nuts there. The squirrels still found those caches about as often as caches whose surroundings were left undisturbed. This result suggests that ______

passages.title: Bite force
passages.text: Although a spotted hyena is smaller than a lion, the bite force of a hyena is greater than ______ lion of comparable age, allowing it to crack bones that lions usually leave behind.

passages.title: Coating tests
passages.text: In the laboratory, one group of engineers sprayed salt water on coated steel panels every hour for six weeks. ______ a second group placed identical panels on a pier by the ocean and checked them once a week for rust.

passages.title: Fresco notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A fifteenth-century fresco covers the walls of a small chapel in central Italy.
• Conservators began restoring it in 2009.
• They removed centuries of grime by hand, a few square centimeters at a time.
• The restoration was completed in 2021.

passages.title: Bacteria experiment
passages.text: Because the samples had been contaminated during shipping ______ the team discarded them and repeated the entire experiment with fresh cultures.

passages.title: Steps by season
passages.text:
A study measured the average number of steps taken per day by adults in three age groups during summer and winter.
Age group | Summer | Winter
20–39 | 8,200 | 7,600
40–59 | 7,500 | 6,700
60 and older | 6,400 | 4,800
The researchers claim that the drop in daily steps from summer to winter was largest for adults aged 60 and older.

passages.title: The rehearsal
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
The orchestra had rehearsed the symphony's final movement eleven times that week. On the twelfth run, the conductor lowered her baton halfway through, said nothing for a long moment, and then told the musicians to go home early. Several of them looked at one another, unsure whether they had played very badly or very well.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: are borrowed from the poets she most admired
candidates.explanation: Work whose rhythms, images and phrases are borrowed from others is "derivative."

A.rationale: "Innovative" means new and original, the opposite of borrowed.

C.rationale: "Obscure" means hard to understand; the text is about borrowing, not difficulty.

D.rationale: "Prolific" means producing a lot; the text says nothing about quantity.

hints: What does the colon's explanation say about the poems?
candidates.remember: Match the word to the explanation after the colon.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: placed some islands dozens of miles from their true positions
candidates.explanation: Charts that misplace and omit islands contain errors: "erroneous."

A.rationale: "Meticulous" means extremely careful, which contradicts the errors described.

B.rationale: "Ornamental" means decorative; the text is about mistakes, not decoration.

C.rationale: "Comprehensive" means complete, but the charts left some islands out.

hints: What kind of problems did the charts have?
candidates.remember: Use the specific details to confirm the word.

candidates.stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the art historian's claim in Text 1?

choices.A: By noting that the sister was abroad and another person likely sat for it
choices.B: By agreeing that the resemblance proves the sitter was the painter's sister
choices.C: By arguing that the portrait was painted much later than 1792
choices.D: By questioning whether the painter knew how to paint portraits

candidates.evidence: the painter's sister spent all of 1791 and 1792 abroad
candidates.explanation: Text 2's letters place the sister abroad and mention a neighbor sitting for the painter in 1792, undercutting the resemblance argument and suggesting an alternative.

B.rationale: The letters show the sister was abroad during the relevant years.

C.rationale: Text 2 does not dispute the date.

D.rationale: Nothing in Text 2 concerns the painter's skill.

hints: What do the letters show about the sister in 1792?

strategy.explanation: Find what Text 2 says that bears on Text 1's claim.

candidates.remember: Documentary evidence can outweigh visual resemblance.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the squirrels forgot where most of their caches were buried.
choices.B: moving landmarks made the squirrels more successful at finding caches.
choices.C: the squirrels did not rely mainly on the nearby stones and logs to locate their caches.
choices.D: the squirrels buried nuts only near large stones and logs.

candidates.evidence: still found those caches about as often
candidates.explanation: Moving the nearby landmarks did not reduce success, so those landmarks were not the main cue the squirrels used.

A.rationale: The squirrels found the moved-landmark caches about as often as the others.

B.rationale: The success rates were about the same, not higher.

D.rationale: The text does not say where the squirrels chose to bury nuts.

hints: What changed, and did success change?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate choices that contradict 'about as often.'

candidates.remember: If changing a factor changes nothing, that factor is not the main cause.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: the bite force of a hyena is greater than
candidates.explanation: The sentence compares one bite force with another, so it needs "that of a lion," not "a lion" itself.

A.rationale: Without "that of," the sentence compares a bite force with a lion.

B.rationale: "Those" is plural, but "bite force" is singular.

C.rationale: "It is for a" does not form a logical comparison with "bite force."

hints: What two things are being compared?

strategy.explanation: Make sure like is compared with like.

candidates.remember: Compare like things: a bite force with a bite force.

author_checklist.hardness: The illogical comparison (bite force vs. lion) sounds natural in speech; most students do not notice it.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.explanation: The two tests ran at the same time in different places, so "Meanwhile" fits.

B.rationale: The second group's work is not a result of the first group's.

C.rationale: The pier test is not an example of the laboratory test.

D.rationale: Nothing in the first sentence makes the second surprising.

hints: Are the two tests happening one after the other, or at the same time?
candidates.remember: Use "meanwhile" for things happening at the same time.

candidates.stem: The student wants to emphasize how long the restoration took. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A fifteenth-century fresco covers the walls of a small chapel in central Italy.
choices.B: Conservators spent twelve years, from 2009 to 2021, restoring the fresco.
choices.C: Conservators removed centuries of grime from the chapel's fifteenth-century fresco.
choices.D: The fresco's restoration was completed in 2021.

candidates.explanation: Only B gives both dates and states the twelve-year span, emphasizing duration.

A.rationale: This describes the fresco, not how long the restoration took.

C.rationale: This describes the work but not its duration.

D.rationale: This gives only the end date, not the length of the project.

hints: Which choice includes both the start and the end?

strategy.explanation: Look for the choice that shows length of time.

candidates.remember: Duration needs a start, an end, or an explicit span.

candidates.subskill: Comma after an introductory dependent clause
candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: Because the samples had been contaminated during
candidates.explanation: "Because the samples had been contaminated during shipping" is a dependent clause introducing the main clause, so a comma follows it.

A.rationale: A semicolon cannot follow a dependent clause; it must separate two independent clauses.

B.rationale: A colon must follow an independent clause, not a dependent "because" clause.

D.rationale: Without a comma, the long introductory clause runs into the main clause.

hints: Is the part before the blank a complete sentence?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate marks that require an independent clause before them.

candidates.remember: A comma follows an introductory dependent clause.

candidates.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researchers' claim?

choices.A: Adults aged 20–39 took the most steps per day in both summer and winter.
choices.B: Adults 60 and older took 4,800 steps per day in winter.
choices.C: Every age group took fewer steps per day in winter than in summer.
choices.D: The oldest group's winter drop (1,600 steps) exceeded the others' (600 and 800).

candidates.evidence: the drop in daily steps from summer to winter was largest
candidates.explanation: The claim compares the size of the drop across groups. D gives all three drops and shows the oldest group's is largest.

A.rationale: This compares totals by age, not the size of the seasonal drop.

B.rationale: A single value cannot show which group's drop was largest.

C.rationale: This shows that all groups dropped, not which dropped most.

hints: What exactly is being compared in the claim?
candidates.remember: Match the evidence to the quantity the claim is about.

candidates.stem: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the musicians?

choices.A: They were certain that the conductor was disappointed.
choices.B: They could not tell how the conductor judged their performance.
choices.C: They wanted to rehearse the movement a thirteenth time.
choices.D: They had stopped playing before the conductor lowered her baton.

candidates.evidence: unsure whether they had played very badly or very well
candidates.explanation: The musicians exchange looks, unsure whether the early dismissal meant failure or success, so they could not read her judgment.

A.rationale: They were "unsure whether they had played very badly or very well."

D.rationale: The conductor stopped them by lowering her baton.

hints: What were the musicians unsure about?
candidates.remember: Inferences about characters must match their stated uncertainty.
